One of the supplied papers does build a benchmark using the British Library BL19 digital collection: “Cultural Analytics for Good: Building Inclusive Evaluation Frameworks for Historical IR” [1]. It uses the BL19 collection (more than 35,000 works from 1700–1899) to construct a benchmark for studying changes in language, terminology, and retrieval in 19th-century fiction and non-fiction, with expert-driven query design and paragraph-level relevance annotation, plus LLM assistance for scalable evaluation [1].

The other supplied papers use different datasets/benchmarks (e.g., map retrieval over Library of Congress images [2], multi-category integrated retrieval [3], CLIR collections [4,9], coverage-focused suites [8], and other domains like dataset search, legal IR, or retrieval efficiency [5,6,10]) [2-10]. None of them appears to target the BL19 retrieval benchmark specifically [2-10].
